items.title: Nvidia’s startup stakes ballooned to $65B, but Huang’s exit puts future deals in doubt
items.description: The value of Nvidia’s private investments has nearly tripled over the past nine months, fueled by Jensen Huang’s aggressive dealmaking and rising valuations of its existing portfolio companies.

items.title: Nvidia promises that revenue will keep soaring — for now
items.description: Despite the turmoil Nvidia is in after the departure of its disgraced founder and CEO Jensen Huang, the company projected that its streak of record-breaking revenue isn't about to stop.

items.title: Nvidia is abandoning China after Jensen Huang’s ouster
items.description: Nvidia's interim CEO says the company is done selling chips to China. How much will that cost?

items.title: Nvidia says its open source AI strategy remains intact after Jensen Huang’s exit
items.description: Nvidia's interim CEO reaffirmed its open source AI strategy and plans to acquire Hugging Face, despite Jensen Huang's sudden departure.

items.title: Nvidia says it doesn’t plan to reappoint Jensen Huang as CEO
items.description: The former CEO offered to return to his top role at the company after his resignation last week.

items.title: Amazon and Google will together own nearly 30% of Anthropic after its IPO
items.description: Amazon will own just under 15% of Anthropic after the IPO, with the option to go much higher. Google is a close second with holdings of nearly 14%.

items.title: China’s Xi calls for removing trade and investment barriers ahead of his meeting with Trump and Putin
items.description: Xi opened the APEC summit in Shenzhen by calling for lower trade and investment barriers, pledging broader access to China’s market and manufacturing sector.

items.title: Iran says army targets U.S. drone and missile sites in Kuwait as Gulf attacks mount
items.description: Iran said its army targeted U.S. drone and missile installations at Kuwait's Ali Al Salem air base, extending a run of attacks on Gulf states.

items.title: Widespread outages hit banks, air travel, the NSA and Apple, disrupting seemingly everything
items.description: Major outages showcase the risks of interconnected tech in the age of AI.

items.title: Putin says EU is losing industry, falling behind competition ahead of meeting with Trump, Xi
items.description: Putin used the speech to emphasize Russia's economic resilience despite U.S. sanctions, and played up opportunities for APEC members in the country.

items.title: Democrat Mary Peltola wins Alaska Senate election
items.description: Peltola's defeat of incumbent Republican Dan Sullivan gives Democrats a solid majority of 56 seats in the Senate as of January.

items.title: Senators press acting U.S. Navy Secretary on Iran war costs, sailor health in confirmation hearing
items.description: Acting Navy Secretary Hung Cao told senators the Navy recoded and used munitions he called expired as the Iran war strains weapons stocks and naval deployments.

items.title: Here’s what happened in crypto today
items.description: Need to know what happened in crypto today? Here is the latest news on daily trends and events impacting Bitcoin price, blockchain, DeFi, Web3 and crypto regulation.

items.title: Ledger hardware implant saga reaches Dubai’s Virgin Megastore
items.description: Two Ledger owners reported losing a combined $604,000 in crypto from hardware wallets they said were purchased at authorized retailer Virgin Megastore in Dubai.

items.title: Nvidia board rejects Huang comeback despite record $116B quarter
items.description: Nvidia beat Wall Street’s revenue expectations by 5.6% and issued a stronger-than-expected sales forecast, while its board resisted growing calls for Jensen Huang’s reinstatement.

items.title: Google finds self-running AI hacking tool with Russian comments in its files
items.description: Google spots an AI that can find and exploit software flaws on its own, no human needed.

items.title: Live updates: Bitcoin stuck near $65,000 as popular 'basis trade' returns dry up
items.description: XRP edged toward $1 and SOL rose 3%, while a Talos report showed crypto’s favorite carry trade now pays about what Treasuries do.

items.title: U.S. judge says Ethereum has ‘no terms of use,’ clears MIT brothers of $25 million fraud
items.description: A federal judge acquitted Anton and James Peraire-Bueno, ruling that their 2023 trade against Ethereum trading bots involved no lie that anyone relied on, and closing the U.S. government’s first criminal case over the practice known as MEV.
